description: Trump signed EO 14399 (91 Fed. Reg. 17125) directing DHS to transmit state citizenship lists by Sept 4, ordering the AG to prioritize prosecuting officials who issue ballots to ineligible voters, and directing a USPS rule under which USPS would not carry ballots for voters absent from state lists.

First Circuit denied a stay of the July 7 final judgment that enjoined most federal defendants (not the President) from implementing EO Sections 2-3 for elections through Nov 3 in 23 states plus DC, noting the government conceded it seeks nationwide enforcement and may use DHS lists for prosecutions of officials.

Supreme Court (6-3, unsigned, three liberal justices dissenting) stayed Judge Talwani's injunction against the EO on ripeness/standing grounds, letting DHS compile citizenship lists, the AG prioritize prosecutions and USPS proceed with rulemaking, while a separate USPS-specific injunction stayed in place.

USPS finalized (published Aug 26) a rule requiring barcoded ballot envelopes and state upload of voter data to a federal ballot-mail portal, with USPS stating it will not deliver ballots for noncompliant states.

After 23-24 states sued over the final USPS rule, Judge Talwani issued a TRO on Aug 27 and a preliminary injunction on Sept 4 barring the government from requiring states to comply with the envelope and portal provisions, and the government sought a Supreme Court stay on Sept 6.

Supreme Court (Alito and Thomas dissenting, Kavanaugh concurring) refused to stay the preliminary injunction, so the USPS ballot-envelope/portal/state-list rule cannot be applied to the Nov 3 midterms, which corrects the prior-context premise that the August ruling left USPS gating in play.

DHS state citizenship lists (due to states by Sept 4 under the EO) are still described as 'coming soon', no court has blocked their creation, DOJ will not say whether they will be released before November, and a Maryland federal judge is set to rule on privacy-law challenges.
DOJ has lost 26 of 31 suits seeking unredacted state voter rolls with no court ordering a handover, and on Oct 9 Judge Sooknanan vacated the DOJ voter-roll initiative (DOJ expected to appeal).

DOJ sued California, Secretary of State Weber and LA County Registrar Logan in federal court in Los Angeles to bar tabulation of mail ballots from about 20,000 voters on a DHS-generated list until citizenship is verified, with no hearing, TRO or ruling reported yet.

DHS Secretary Mullin said ICE agents could enter polling places to make arrests only for a threat to the site or to serve a warrant, while a DHS spokesperson said ICE is not planning operations targeting polling locations.

Denver, LULAC, Common Cause and UnidosUS sued DHS in D.D.C. to bar armed federal agents near open polling places and drop boxes under the federal ban on troops or armed men at elections, with no merits ruling found (per search-result summary; the Stateline page returned 403).

Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine told Sen. Slotkin in a letter reported by AP that the Joint Force has no plans to send federal military or federalized Guard to polling places or to seize ballots or machines, and expects no unlawful order on the midterms.

Photos showed Guard members near a Foggy Bottom ballot drop box in DC (2,978 Guard troops in the city as of Oct 5), the DC Board of Elections asked the Guard to limit placement near drop boxes, and JTF-DC said its troops are directed not to monitor or secure polling locations; DC is not a competitive-scorecard state.

AAG Dhillon announced about 1,000 DOJ election monitors for November without naming jurisdictions, saying DOJ is weighing places where it believes voter fraud may occur, and Votebeat reports the plan also includes FBI command posts.

FBI Director Patel told the Senate Judiciary Committee he would not commit to keeping agents away from polling places, while the Padilla/Durbin/Whitehouse letter says he pledged at the same hearing not to seize ballots or machines before certification.

Senators Padilla, Durbin and Whitehouse demanded Blanche commit not to seize ballots or equipment, citing removal of DOJ's Election Crimes Manual from its website, a suspended Justice Manual consultation requirement, and personal calls from Trump to DOJ attorneys about election investigations.
The FBI executed a search warrant at the Fulton County elections hub and seized more than 650 boxes of 2020 ballots and records, a federal action touching 2020 materials rather than 2026 ballots.

Nevada's Secretary of State said his office received seven FBI voter-related subpoenas over about three months after a federal court sided with Nevada in August in DOJ's suit for the full voter list (per CNN via KRDO and a search summary).

On the day absentee ballots were first mailed, the Republican-majority NC State Board of Elections voted 3-2 to require disqualification of mail ballots returned in unsealed envelopes, limit who may return a voter's ballot to close relatives or guardians, and lift its ban on signature matching, and these rules are in force pending litigation with no rejections yet reported.

Judge Schroeder (M.D.N.C.) heard on Oct 14 a preliminary-injunction motion by civil-rights groups against the Sept 4 memos (RNC and NCGOP allowed to intervene; plaintiffs say thousands, one report 4,000+, of ballots would be invalidated), said he would rule quickly, and no ruling was found as of Oct 16.

The Third Circuit's 2025 Eakin ruling bars counties from rejecting mail ballots for missing or wrong envelope dates, the Supreme Court in June 2026 invited the Solicitor General's views on review, and a separate Pennsylvania Supreme Court state-law challenge is pending, so no decision restricting acceptance is in force as retrieved.

Ohio SB 293 (signed Dec 19, 2025; effective March 19, 2026) ended the four-day post-Election Day receipt grace period for mailed absentee ballots except military and overseas voters, a state rule now in force for the midterms (per search-result summary).

In Watson v. RNC (decided June 29, 2026, Barrett writing) the Supreme Court held federal Election Day statutes do not preempt state rules counting timely-cast mail ballots received after Election Day, reversing the Fifth Circuit.

California rejected 148,241 mail ballots (1.73%, up from 1.56% in the 2024 primary, 93,479 for lateness) in its June 2026 primary, and Oregon and Washington also reported higher late-postmark rejections, which experts link to USPS postmark and pickup changes rather than to the EO or a state rule change, and none of these are scorecard states.

The Georgia Supreme Court heard argument on whether Fulton County must seat two Republican nominees (one of whom refused to certify the 2024 primary) on its election board, with a ruling expected by end of March 2027 and Georgia appeals courts having held that board members must certify results.

USPS finalized (published Aug 26) a rule requiring barcoded ballot envelopes and state upload of voter data to a federal ballot-mail portal, with USPS stating it will not deliver ballots for noncompliant states.

After 23-24 states sued over the final USPS rule, Judge Talwani issued a TRO on Aug 27 and a preliminary injunction on Sept 4 barring the government from requiring states to comply with the envelope and portal provisions, and the government sought a Supreme Court stay on Sept 6.

Supreme Court (Alito and Thomas dissenting, Kavanaugh concurring) refused to stay the preliminary injunction, so the USPS ballot-envelope/portal/state-list rule cannot be applied to the Nov 3 midterms, which corrects the prior-context premise that the August ruling left USPS gating in play.

DHS state citizenship lists (due to states by Sept 4 under the EO) are still described as 'coming soon', no court has blocked their creation, DOJ will not say whether they will be released before November, and a Maryland federal judge is set to rule on privacy-law challenges. DOJ has lost 26 of 31 suits seeking unredacted state voter rolls with no court ordering a handover, and on Oct 9 Judge Sooknanan vacated the DOJ voter-roll initiative (DOJ expected to appeal).

DHS Secretary Mullin said ICE agents could enter polling places to make arrests only for a threat to the site or to serve a warrant, while a DHS spokesperson said ICE is not planning operations targeting polling locations.

Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine told Sen. Slotkin in a letter reported by AP that the Joint Force has no plans to send federal military or federalized Guard to polling places or to seize ballots or machines, and expects no unlawful order on the midterms.

AAG Dhillon announced about 1,000 DOJ election monitors for November without naming jurisdictions, saying DOJ is weighing places where it believes voter fraud may occur, and Votebeat reports the plan also includes FBI command posts.

Voting-rights groups sued in Bexar County district court over more than 500,000 DPS-portal voter registrations never processed due to a software error, seeking enforcement of a 2021 settlement before Nov 3, with no ruling or state response found.

New Hampshire appealed to the Supreme Court after the First Circuit upheld election officials' discretion to consider student IDs, asking the Court to bar any consideration of student IDs for the midterms.
Per Hoodline and Courthouse News, plaintiffs waited 18 days after the Sept 4 vote; the denial is of preliminary relief only and merits remain pending.

Trump signed EO 14399 (91 Fed. Reg. 17125) directing DHS to transmit state citizenship lists by Sept 4, ordering the AG to prioritize prosecuting officials who issue ballots to ineligible voters, and directing a USPS rule under which USPS would not carry ballots for voters absent from state lists.

First Circuit denied a stay of the July 7 final judgment that enjoined most federal defendants (not the President) from implementing EO Sections 2-3 for elections through Nov 3 in 23 states plus DC, noting the government conceded it seeks nationwide enforcement and may use DHS lists for prosecutions of officials.

USPS finalized (published Aug 26) a rule requiring barcoded ballot envelopes and state upload of voter data to a federal ballot-mail portal, with USPS stating it will not deliver ballots for noncompliant states.

After 23-24 states sued over the final USPS rule, Judge Talwani issued a TRO on Aug 27 and a preliminary injunction on Sept 4 barring the government from requiring states to comply with the envelope and portal provisions, and the government sought a Supreme Court stay on Sept 6.

Supreme Court (Alito and Thomas dissenting, Kavanaugh concurring) refused to stay the preliminary injunction, so the USPS ballot-envelope/portal/state-list rule cannot be applied to the Nov 3 midterms, which corrects the prior-context premise that the August ruling left USPS gating in play.

DHS state citizenship lists (due to states by Sept 4 under the EO) are still described as 'coming soon', no court has blocked their creation, DOJ will not say whether they will be released before November, and a Maryland federal judge is set to rule on privacy-law challenges.
